stories.headline: Rajnath Singh meets US Secy of War Hegseth on sidelines of ASEAN defence ministers’ meeting in Philippines
stories.title: Rajnath Singh meets US Secy of War Hegseth on sidelines of ASEAN defence ministers’ meeting in Philippines
stories.summary: Philippines, October 28 : Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Wednesday met US War Secretary Pete Hegseth on sidelines of the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu, Philippines. The Defence Minister is also scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from the United States, Japan, Australia and from other participating nations. The US War Secretary said during the meeting, the counterparts "celebrated the one-year anniversary of the Framework for our Major Defense Partnership and explored ways to strengthen cooperation." In a post on X, Pete Hegseth said, "Great meeting with Indian Minister of Defence Singh. We celebrated the one-year anniversary of the Framework for our Major Defense Partnership and explored ways to strengthen cooperation." The meeting comes as after the meeting in 2025, both leaders signed the ‘framework for the US-India major defence partnership’. The 2025 framework marked a new chapter to further transform the partnership over the next 10 years. According to the Ministry of Defence, it is intended to provide a unified vision and policy direction to deepen defence cooperation. Meanwhile, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth also met representatives from South Korea, Australia and Japan. For his meeting with South Korean Defence Minister Kang, he said, "Great meeting with ROK Minister of National Defense Kang at ADMM-Plus. The U.S.-ROK Alliance is built on peace through strength—ready forces, decisive capability, and combined lethality that deters aggression. America stands with allies that are serious about their own defense." For his meeting with Australian Deputy Prime Minister Marles, he said," It was a pleasure to meet with Australian Deputy Prime Minister Marles. Together, we are optimizing the Alliance to strengthen deterrence and deliver results." For his meeting with Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi, he said, " I met with Japan’s Minister of Defense Shinjirō Koizumi @shinjirokoiz to advance our shared vision of peace through strength. Our strategic alignment is essential to building a credible denial defense—supported by increased investment, greater access, more realistic training, and stronger production of the munitions our forces need." The developments come as Rajnath Singh arrived in Cebu, on Tuesday night to attend the ADMM-Plus, where he will address shared regional and international security issues. Upon his arrival at Cebu airport, Singh received a ceremonial welcome from M Gen Fabian M Pedregosa PAF (Retd), Undersecretary of the Department of National Defence of the Philippines. Indian Ambassador to the Philippines Harsh Kumar Jain and Defence Attaché Captain ChandraKant Kothari were also present to welcome the Defence Minister. Singh later interacted with members of the Indian community and Filipino nationals upon arriving at his hotel. On Thursday, the Defence Minister will represent India at the ADMM-Plus meeting and address the forum on common regional and international security challenges. Before departing for Cebu, Singh reiterated India's commitment to strengthening its engagement with ASEAN and promoting stability across the Indo-Pacific region. In a post on X, he said, “India is firmly committed to ASEAN centrality and the peace, stability, and collective growth of the Indo-Pacific region under our Act East Policy.” On the sidelines of the meeting, Singh is scheduled to hold bilateral discussions with defence counterparts from several participating countries, including the host nation, the Philippines, as well as the United States, Japan, Australia, Singapore, Vietnam and South Korea. (ANI)

Powerful tidal surges and intense coastal erosion completely washed away major portions of the scenic road, entirely severing connectivity to the local fishing harbour and dozens of nearby coastal villages.

State disaster management chief Prakhar Jain confirmed the widespread infrastructure damage, noting, "The cyclone brought heavy to very heavy rainfall, triggering widespread disruption in affected areas.
Damage assessments are fully underway".

The Andhra Pradesh state government has put the district on high alert and immediately deployed emergency restoration teams to repair the coastal artery.

article_sentences: Fishermen of this coastal town of Thoothukudi abstained from fishing for the second consecutive day on Tuesday (October 27, 2027) following warning on Cyclone ‘Arnab’.

As the India Meteorological Department had warned that the sea would be rough in the wake of the cyclone in the Bay of Bengal, the boats involved in deep sea fishing have been urged to return to the shore immediately.
Fishermen operating the mechanised boats from Thoothukudi Fishing Harbour did not go venture into the sea on Monday.
They abstained from fishing for the second day on Tuesday as there was no improvement in the weather.
Only a few fishermen from Terespuram and New Harbour Beach ventured into the sea on country boats in areas closer to the shore and returned with small catch.

The New Harbour Beach fishermen tested their fortune with ‘Karai Madi’ (shore net), which is cast in the sea at a distance from the shore from a boat and is retrieved by more than 30 people standing on the shore.
After hours of toiling in dragging the fishnet, the fishermen had to be content with around 350 kg sardines, smaller trevally, and white snapper fishes.

stories.headline: Heavy rain alert for 9 Jharkhand districts amid cyclone Arnab
stories.title: Heavy rain alert for 9 Jharkhand districts amid cyclone Arnab
stories.summary: Ranchi, Oct 28 : Weather conditions have changed across Jharkhand under the influence of the severe cyclonic storm 'Arnab', which originated in the Bay of Bengal. Several parts of the state, including the capital Ranchi, have been witnessing rainfall since Wednesday morning, prompting the India Meteorological Department (IMD) to issue a heavy rainfall warning for nine districts. The IMD has warned of heavy rainfall in Ranchi, Khunti, Simdega, Gumla, Lohardaga, Bokaro, Seraikela-Kharsawan, and East and West Singhbhum districts. The impact of the cyclone is also expected to bring down temperatures across Jharkhand by around three to four degrees Celsius. In view of the prevailing weather conditions and the possibility of further deterioration, authorities have ordered the suspension of classes from kindergarten (KG) to Class 12 in Ranchi and Lohardaga districts on October 28 and 29 as a precautionary measure. In Ranchi, intermittent showers have continued since Wednesday morning, while the sky remains overcast. Rainfall accompanied by strong winds has brought a noticeable change in the weather, with temperatures dropping across the city. Similar conditions have been reported from several other parts of Jharkhand, including Hazaribagh, Koderma, Chaibasa, Deoghar, Giridih and Bokaro, where cloudy skies and rainfall have affected normal weather conditions. Meteorological Department scientist Abhishek Anand explained that Jharkhand's geographical location means the Singhbhum region is likely to experience the cyclone's effects first. Thereafter, rainfall and strong winds may spread to other parts of the state, depending on the storm's movement and intensity. The Meteorological Department has urged residents to remain vigilant, particularly in areas where heavy rainfall is expected. Cyclone 'Arnab' reached the Andhra Pradesh coast early Wednesday morning. According to the department's forecast, the cyclone was expected to cross the coast south of Yanam, between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam. During the landfall period, sustained wind speeds were projected to reach 125–135 kmph, while gusts could touch 150 kmph. Amid the changing weather conditions, Ranchi Deputy Commissioner Manjunath Bhajantri convened a meeting with officials from the departments concerned and issued directions to ensure preparedness and a prompt response to any weather-related emergencies. As part of the precautionary arrangements, the electricity department's control room and the Ranchi Municipal Corporation's rapid response team have been placed on alert. The teams have been instructed to respond immediately to incidents such as power supply disruptions and waterlogging caused by heavy rainfall or strong winds. The Railways has also initiated precautionary measures in anticipation of the cyclone's impact. According to information released by the Railways, the operations of at least half a dozen trains either originating from Jharkhand or passing through the state have been cancelled in view of the prevailing conditions. The administration has appealed to residents to take necessary precautions during thunderstorms and periods of strong winds. Commuters have also been urged to exercise caution while travelling on roads affected by waterlogging and to remain alert to changing conditions. The public has been asked to follow weather warnings issued by the Meteorological Department and comply with instructions from the local administration to minimise the risk of accidents and other emergencies. Farmers, meanwhile, have been advised to shift harvested crops and other agricultural produce to safe locations to protect them from rain and strong winds. --IANS

stories.headline: Andhra reports no casualties after cyclone Arnab, says CM Naidu
stories.title: Andhra reports no casualties after cyclone Arnab, says CM Naidu
stories.summary: Amaravati, Oct 28 : Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu on Wednesday said no loss of life has been reported so far following Cyclone Arnab, crediting advance precautionary measures taken by the administration for preventing casualties. Speaking during a teleconference with 32,000 personnel, including district collectors, the Chief Minister directed officials to minimise property damage and restore normalcy in cyclone-affected areas at the earliest. "No loss of life has been reported so far due to Cyclone Arnab. The advance precautionary measures taken by the administrative machinery helped prevent casualties," said Naidu in an official press release. The CM instructed officials to clear roads blocked by fallen trees within two hours and ensure immediate removal of trees obstructing national highways. Also, he directed them to restore electricity supply in affected areas once strong winds subsided. Naidu stressed the need to provide adequate food, drinking water and medical facilities at cyclone shelters and asked officials to prevent water from entering agricultural fields, protect horticultural crops and take measures to prevent breaches in tanks and canals. The CM asked officials to prepare preliminary estimates of crop damage and keep National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) personnel on standby. Further, the officials were directed to make full use of the Manamitra system to address public grievances in cyclone-affected areas and ensure that complainants were informed about the action taken to resolve their issues. Meanwhile, Kakinada Superintendent of Police (SP) G Bindu Madhav said, "Cyclone Arnab had significantly affected the district, uprooting a few hundred trees and fewer than 100 electric poles. However, no major damage has been reported and rainfall subsided after 1 am." Madhav said people were evacuated to relief camps as a precautionary measure and remained there due to the strong winds and roar of the storm between midnight and 1 am. The Uppada road, running along the coast, has been completely washed away, he said, adding that rainfall was relatively low in the district with gusty winds causing the main impact. Alluri Sitaramaraju district SP Amit Bardar said the Cyclone had limited impact on the district, as of 9 am, with trees and electric poles uprooted and some roads inundated. "No loss of life or major damage to infrastructure, houses or livestock has been reported so far. We are monitoring the situation closely as water levels may rise due to continued rainfall," Bardar told PTI. An old bridge in Tadiguda village of Anantagiri mandal was washed away, isolating a hamlet, said the SP, adding that alternative arrangements were being made and restoration work was underway. The preliminary assessment indicated limited overall impact, though the situation would continue to be monitored as rainfall persisted, he added. Konaseema district SP Rahul Meena said gusty winds reaching up 130 kmph had uprooted trees and electric poles across the district during the Cyclone late on Tuesday night. No casualties or property damage had been reported. Fallen trees and electric poles had blocked roads and disrupted power supply, he said, adding that electricity connections were expected to be restored by within few hours, while major highways would be cleared within two to three hours. "Konaseema is among the worst-affected districts, with winds reaching up to 130 kmph uprooting trees and electric poles, blocking roads and disrupting power supply," the SP told PTI. Clearance of interior roads could take until evening, he said, adding that wind speeds had reduced and the cyclone had moved towards Kakinada after weakening slightly. More than 10,000 people had been evacuated from low-lying areas and shifted to shelters, according to his preliminary information. Around 495 cyclone shelters and temporary relief centres had been set up. No village inundation had been reported and water accumulated due to the storm surge had drained, he said. Two NDRF teams and as many SDRF teams were deployed a day before the cyclone to conduct road clearance and rescue operations in response to emergency calls, he said. Additional Andhra Pradesh Special Police (APSP) platoons had also been deployed for clearance operations and other tasks, he said, adding that personnel from various departments were working continuously to restore normalcy by evening. PTI

article_sentences: The cyclone is expected to bring maximum sustained wind speeds of 125-135 kmph, gusting to 150 kmph, the IMD said in a press release.

New Delhi: Delhi-NCR is likely to witness a change in weather conditions, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasting isolated to scattered rainfall across the national capital from October 28 to November 1 under the influence of a western disturbance and very severe Cyclone Arnab.
The unseasonal rainfall is expected to bring a significant drop in daytime temperatures, potentially affecting Karwa Chauth celebrations.
The forecast comes as northern and eastern India brace for rainfall over the coming days.

According to the IMD, a western disturbance, in the form of a cyclonic circulation, lies over northwest Uttar Pradesh and its neighbourhood, influencing weather conditions across parts of north India.

Meanwhile, Cyclone Arnab is likely to move northwestwards and cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam, as a very severe cyclonic storm by the forenoon of October 28.
The weather agency has also forecast isolated to very heavy rainfall over Telangana and Vidarbha on October 28, followed by Chhattisgarh, east Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand and Odisha on October 29.
Bihar is likely to experience rainfall between October 29 and 30.

Meanwhile, Delhi's air quality remained in the 'poor' category on Wednesday morning, with the city-level Air Quality Index (AQI) reaching 250 at 8 a.m., according to the Central Pollution Control Board's (CPCB) All India AQI portal.
PM2.5, fine particulate matter capable of penetrating deep into the lungs, was identified as the prominent pollutant.
Among the monitoring stations, Vivek Vihar recorded the highest AQI at 320, followed by Jahangirpuri at 307 and Patparganj at 291.
Sirifort recorded an AQI of 290, while Dwarka Sector 8 registered 286.

article_sentences: Sivasagar — In a major push toward climate resilience and economic rehabilitation, the Assam Government has distributed approximately 2.4 lakh high-yielding coconut and arecanut seedlings to flood-affected farmers.
The distribution drive, targeting the severely hit Sivasagar and Charaideo districts, aims to help over 50,000 farmers recover from devastating monsoon damages.

Handing over the saplings at a public event at the Boarding Playground, Agriculture and Irrigation Minister Pijush Hazarika detailed the state's vision to transform Assam into a horticultural powerhouse.
The initial phase delivered 80,000 coconut and 1.6 lakh arecanut plants to promote immediate crop diversification.
State-wide, the annual target stands at 2.84 lakh coconut and 8 lakh arecanut saplings.
Minister Hazarika announced that the government is aggressively working to double its active irrigation network, significantly reducing agrarian dependence on erratic rainfall.

Flanked by Water Resources Minister Susanta Borgohain and MLA Akhil Gogoi, Hazarika also assured farmers that adequate seeds and technical inputs are secured for the upcoming Rabi cropping season to guarantee sustainable rural livelihoods.

stories.headline: Israel election: exit polls point to no clear winner or majority
stories.title: Israel election: exit polls point to no clear winner or majority
stories.summary: Jerusalem, Oct 28 : Israel's parliamentary election appeared to have produced no clear winner, with exit polls indicating that both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc and the opposition alliance seeking to replace him had fallen short of the 61 seats required for a majority in the 120-member Knesset. According to The Jerusalem Post, the exit polls projected Netanyahu's bloc to secure 51-52 seats, while the opposition bloc, comprising Yashar, B'Yachad, Yisrael Beytenu and the Democrats, was expected to win 49-51 seats. Channels 11 and 13 projected both sides to be tied at 51 seats each, while Channel 12's survey gave Netanyahu's bloc a slight edge with 52 seats. The opposition bloc declared victory shortly after the exit poll results were released, although neither side appeared to have a clear route to forming a government. The exit polls also indicated that the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot, a former chief of staff of the Israel Defence Forces, could emerge with a slight advantage over Netanyahu's right-wing and far-right coalition in terms of the combined strength of its constituent parties. However, Netanyahu's Likud was projected to remain the single largest party, with around 27 seats, while Yashar was forecast to win 21-22 seats. The results suggested that Netanyahu continued to retain the support of a substantial core of Likud voters despite widespread opposition to his leadership among sections of the Israeli electorate. Nevertheless, the projected seat distribution indicated that his ability to form another coalition government could be constrained by the opposition's combined strength and the potential influence of smaller parties. The election witnessed a historic voter turnout and was described by some as one of the most consequential in Israel's history. It was also marked by record participation among Israeli Arab voters, adding another significant dimension to the electoral contest. Exit polls projected that Israeli Arab parties could collectively secure as many as 18 seats in the Knesset, potentially giving them considerable leverage during the negotiations to form the next government. article_sentences: The State Election Commission has released draft rolls for 209 newly delimited KMC wards, but Opposition parties have questioned the November 12 deadline amid concerns over more than one lakh voter cases.

Kolkata: Nearly 32 lakh voters, 209 newly delimited wards, and more than one lakh disputed voter cases have put Kolkata’s municipal election preparations under scrutiny, with Opposition parties questioning whether the electoral machinery has enough time to resolve discrepancies before it publishes the final rolls.

The State Election Commission has circulated draft electoral rolls and proposed polling-station layouts for all 209 wards of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC), setting November 12 as the deadline for filing claims and objections.
However, the release of the draft documents has done little to ease concerns over voter verification, pending tribunal cases and the impact of electoral-roll revisions.
The controversy has also brought election timing into sharper focus.

Opposition parties have sought to postpone the civic polls, arguing that the exercise should not proceed until the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process and the Special Summary Revision announced by the Election Commission of India are complete.

The draft rolls and proposed booth arrangements were presented to political parties at the New Administrative Building in Alipore by senior officials of the South 24-Parganas district administration, led by the additional district magistrate.
The draft electoral rolls cover nearly 32 lakh voters across the 209 wards.

While the publication marks a step towards preparing for the civic elections, Opposition representatives have questioned whether the schedule allows sufficient time to scrutinise the changes and establish the status of voters whose cases remain unresolved.
Their concerns centre on the combined workload arising from ward delimitation, voter-roll revision and the allocation of polling stations.
With November 12 as the deadline, parties argue that officials must verify voter movements, identify discrepancies and address pending appeals within a compressed timeframe.
They have described examining the changes and correcting thousands of discrepancies in just over two weeks as logistically impossible.

stories.title: More than 100 people killed in Sudanese army drone attack on market, says Sudanese rights group
stories.summary: Shendi, Oct 28: More than 100 people were killed in a Sudanese military drone strike on a busy market in Nyala, the capital city of the South Darfur province in southwestern Sudan, said Emergency Lawyers, a rights group tracking violence in the country, in a statement Tuesday. The strike, which it says happened Monday evening, also injured 113 people. The group said many of those killed and injured were women and children. The group blamed the Sudanese military for the strike on the market, condemning the attack. “This massacre transformed a civilian marketplace into a scene of mass killing and injury and is an assault that threatens the lives of residents and compounds their suffering amid the ongoing war,” the group said in a statement. It called for an independent investigation into the strike. Doctors Without Borders, which is also known as Médecins Sans Frontières, or MSF, said earlier that 36 bodies arrived at its hospital in Nyala and reported seeing 150 injured in its emergency room. Nyala, the capital of South Darfur province, is controlled by the paramilitary group Rapid Support Forces, which has been fighting with the Sudanese army since 2023. Drone warfare has been a staple of this war but in recent weeks, a massive escalation of drone strikes by both the RSF and the Sudanese army has killed hundreds. Both warring parties have increasingly launched explosive-laden drones that, in multiple cases, targeted civilian infrastructure, including hospitals, dams, schools, markets and displacement camps. Drone strikes have become the deadliest threat to civilians in this conflict, according to the UN. The conflict has created the world's largest humanitarian crisis, with about 34 million people — almost two out of every three Sudanese — needing assistance, according to the UN. Sudan's war started in April 2023 when tensions between the military and the RSF exploded into open fighting in the capital, Khartoum, and spread across the country. Previous strike leaves parts of Sudan without power Large parts of Sudan's capital were without electricity for more than 12 hours Tuesday after a drone strike on a major power substation, according to an electric company official. The attack left hospitals and bakeries dependent on generators and limited water supplies across Khartoum. The state-run Sudanese Electricity Distribution Company acknowledged “serious damage and technical faults” to the distribution network and several main stations and power lines but didn't explain the reason in a statement. It apologized to residents across Khartoum state for repeated and prolonged outages. A company official, speaking to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because he was not authorized to speak to the media, said a drone attack hit the Al-Markhiyat transformer station in Omdurman, on the outskirts of Khartoum. He said it is the second to hit the station this year, blaming it on the country's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. The RSF has been at war with the Sudanese military for more than three years. Sudan's war began in April 2023, when simmering tensions between the military and the RSF exploded into open fighting in Khartoum and spread across the country. Deadly drone attacks across Sudan have been carried out by the two rival forces. But those attacks have become rare in Khartoum since the Sudanese military took control of the capital in May 2025, after years of brutal fighting between the military and the RSF. The UN has expressed concern over the use of drones across Sudan, saying they have been killing civilians, including children, and are disrupting essential services. The official who spoke to AP said technical teams are still assessing the damage, describing the strike as major. He estimated that 60 per cent of the power supply in the capital could be affected, predicting that water stations will be most affected. A resident living near the Al-Markhiyat transformer station in Omdurman said he heard a drone shortly before the blast. “At around 4:30 in the morning, on my way to dawn prayers, I heard the sound of a drone very close by, and just moments later a huge explosion, and the power went out,” Abdel-Hafiz Abdel-Mutaal told AP. “I saw fire burning at the transformer station.” The city descended into darkness after sundown. Adel Ali, a resident of south Khartoum, said he was without power and water for 17 hours. “My main concern is how to preserve my insulin supply which needs a fridge,” Ali, a diabetes patient, said. “Life without electricity is totally paralyzed, and a bread crisis is emerging as many bakeries have shut down.” He said this would drive the price of bread even higher. The electricity company, in its statement, said power rationing would be longer than usual in all areas until repairs are finished. It did not say when that would be. Technical teams were working around the clock to restore power, it added. The conflict has killed at least 59,000 people, according to conflict monitor ACLED, though aid groups say the true toll is likely higher. Over 67 per cent of the country's population is dependent on aid, while 825,000 children face acute malnutrition. The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification, or IPC, a global food crisis monitor, warned last week that the “deteriorating humanitarian situation” across greater Darfur and Kordofan states is worsening, with food insecurity putting these areas at risk of famine. In a joint statement, over 30 countries, including the United States, United Kingdom and the European Commission, urged parties to the conflict in the country “to lift all impediments on humanitarian assistance.”

stories.title: CERC Proposes Allowing Pumped Storage Plants to Participate in High-Price Power Market
stories.summary: The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) has proposed allowing pumped storage plants (PSPs) to participate in the High Price Day Ahead Market (HP-DAM), potentially providing storage developers with an additional avenue to sell electricity during periods of high demand and prices. In an order, the commission proposed including PSPs as an eligible category of generating stations in the existing HP-DAM segment on power exchanges. The commission has initiated suo motu proceedings on the proposal and invited written submissions from parties within 15 days of the order. The proposal follows recommendations from the National Load Despatch Centre (NLDC) and a suggestion from the Ministry of Power to consider allowing PSPs to participate in the high-price market segment. CERC said the existing Day Ahead Market (DAM) alone may not provide sufficient commercial opportunities for pumped storage projects under prevailing market conditions. Participation in HP-DAM could improve their commercial viability by allowing them to access periods of higher demand and prices. The commission also noted that greater participation by pumped storage plants could improve the utilisation of flexible storage resources during periods of constrained power supply, supporting grid flexibility. India has 7.4 GW of operational pumped storage capacity According to an analysis submitted by NLDC, India had 7,425.6 MW of operational pumped storage capacity, comprising 4,845.6 MW of on-stream projects and 2,580 MW of off-stream projects, based on a Central Electricity Authority (CEA) report published in January 2026. Another 15,870 MW of PSP capacity was under construction, while the country's estimated pumped storage potential stood at approximately 290.2 GW. NLDC noted that operational pumped storage plants were almost fully tied up, leaving limited merchant capacity among operational inter-state transmission system-connected projects. Allowing PSPs with merchant capacity to participate in HP-DAM could provide an additional market for energy arbitrage during periods of high-price discovery. ALSO READ: Australia Walks Away From 7.2 GWh of Pumped Hydro. India Is Planning 100 GW Solar and evening peak prices offer arbitrage opportunity The commission's proposal is supported by NLDC's analysis of market-clearing prices between April 2025 and July 2026, which identified a substantial difference between electricity prices during solar generation hours and evening peak demand. According to the analysis, average unconstrained market-clearing prices in the Day Ahead Market were approximately ₹2.20 per unit during solar hours and ₹6.57 per unit during evening peak hours. The resulting price differential of around ₹4.37 per unit indicates a potential arbitrage opportunity for pumped storage projects, subject to project-specific costs and operating conditions. Pumped storage plants use electricity to pump water to an upper reservoir when power is relatively inexpensive and generate electricity by releasing the stored water when demand and prices are higher. However, NLDC's analysis also highlighted the limited liquidity of the existing HP-DAM segment. Between April 2025 and July 2026, market clearing occurred on 47 days, or 9.65% of the analysis period, and across 965 time blocks, accounting for 2.06% of the period. While HP-DAM recorded higher price discovery than the regular DAM during certain intervals, the commission noted that actual revenue realisation would depend on both the prices discovered and the volume of electricity successfully cleared. Pumped storage costs could affect commercial viability NLDC's assessment also examined the costs associated with pumped storage projects. The levelised fixed-cost component of PSP tariffs was estimated at approximately ₹3.30-4.98 per unit, while the effective landed tariff, including pumping costs, could reach ₹8.92 per unit, depending on project-specific characteristics and operating assumptions. The order cited several examples of approved or discovered tariffs, including ₹6.69 per unit for Greenko's 500 MW/3,000 MWh standalone storage project awarded by NTPC Renewable Energy Ltd in December 2022, based on the effective storage cost under a two charge-discharge cycle operation. These figures indicate that the commercial case for participation in high-price markets will depend on project costs, pumping expenses, market prices and the availability of trading opportunities. CERC initiates proceedings on proposed inclusion HP-DAM was introduced under the Integrated Day Ahead Market framework to provide a trading avenue for generating stations with high generation costs that could face constraints under the prevailing price ceiling in the regular DAM. The eligible categories currently include gas-based generating stations using imported regasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) and naphtha, imported coal-based generating stations using only imported coal, and battery energy storage systems (BESS). The Ministry of Power's guidelines for promoting pumped storage projects, issued in April 2023, had provided for PSPs and other storage projects to participate in all power exchange market segments, including HP-DAM, to take advantage of price differences between peak and off-peak periods. CERC's latest order proposes extending the existing eligibility framework to pumped storage plants. The commission has directed parties to submit their written representations within 15 days, with further proceedings to follow under Regulation 56 of the Conduct of Business Regulations, 2023.
